root_cause.text: The vulnerability occurs because the set clone operation was performed unconditionally during any NFT_ITER_UPDATE walk (including set deletion and release paths), and a memory allocation failure during cloning triggered a WARN splat in nft_map_deactivate, even though cloning was unnecessary in those contexts.
root_cause.evidence: The patch introduces NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE to restrict set cloning to only the flush set command in the preparation phase, and modifies the pipapo and rbtree backends to only clone when this iteration type is used. The commit message explicitly states "Restrict set clone to the flush set command in the preparation phase" and "After this update, there is no need to clone a set that is being deleted, this includes bound anonymous set." The WARN splat was triggered by a failing GFP_KERNEL allocation in the clone path during `nft_map_deactivate`, which is called from set release paths.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE enum value to support cloning the set before iteration for element updates.
intent_record.what: Added a new enum member NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE to nft_iter_type in include/net/netfilter/nft_set.h, along with a comment describing it as 'clone set before iteration under mutex to update element'.
intent_record.how: Defines a new iteration type that, when used, will trigger cloning of the set before iterating under a mutex to update elements. Currently no code uses it, so behavior is unchanged.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add explanatory comment to nft_map_deactivate to clarify iterator usage rationale.
intent_record.what: Added a multi-line comment before nft_map_deactivate explaining why it uses NFT_ITER_UPDATE iterator even during preparation phase.
intent_record.how: No change in runtime behavior; the comment provides documentation for future maintainers.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use clone iterator type to allow set backend to safely clone during flush preparation.
intent_record.what: Changed the iterator type in nft_set_flush from NFT_ITER_UPDATE to NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE and added a comment explaining that the set backend may need to clone the set during preparation.
intent_record.how: The flush operation now uses an iterator that works on a clone of the set, ensuring safe handling when the backend needs to clone the set during the preparation phase, preventing potential race conditions or data corruption.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add handling for NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE in nft_rhash_walk to apply the same skip check warning as for NFT_ITER_UPDATE.
intent_record.what: Added a new case label 'NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE' to the switch statement in nft_rhash_walk, placed before the existing 'NFT_ITER_UPDATE' case so that both share the same code block (including the WARN_ON_ONCE call).
intent_record.how: When iter->type is NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE, the function now executes the same WARN_ON_ONCE(iter->skip != 0) check as for NFT_ITER_UPDATE, ensuring the invariant is enforced for this new iterator type.

intent_record.intent_summary: Refactor the pipapo set walk function to distinguish between update walks that require cloning and those that do not, improving performance by avoiding unnecessary allocations and clarifying the locking requirements.
intent_record.what: Modified the switch statement in nft_pipapo_walk to separate the case for NFT_ITER_UPDATE into two cases: NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE (which clones the set) and NFT_ITER_UPDATE (which uses an existing clone or the protected match under the transaction mutex).
intent_record.how: The change alters how the walk function selects the match to traverse: for NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE, it clones the set (fallible); for NFT_ITER_UPDATE, it uses priv->clone if available, otherwise the protected match with a mutex assertion. This avoids unnecessary cloning when not required and adds a lock check.

intent_record.intent_summary: Separate the array resize check for cloned updates from regular updates by introducing a dedicated NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE case with fallthrough.
intent_record.what: Added a new case 'NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE' before 'NFT_ITER_UPDATE' in the switch statement of nft_rbtree_walk, which includes the array resize check and a fallthrough to the NFT_ITER_UPDATE case; the NFT_ITER_UPDATE case now only contains the lockdep assertion and the walk call.
intent_record.how: The walk function now handles a new iteration type NFT_ITER_UPDATE_CLONE that performs the array resize check before falling through to execute the same update walk logic (including lockdep assertion) as NFT_ITER_UPDATE, while the existing NFT_ITER_UPDATE case no longer performs the resize check.

candidates.rationale: Sets the iterator type to NFT_ITER_UPDATE unconditionally in nft_set_flush, which triggers cloning in the set backend even when flushing (a deletion path) does not require cloned data. This unnecessary clone operation can fail with -ENOMEM, leading to a WARN splat.

Performs the clone unconditionally for any NFT_ITER_UPDATE walk, including deletion and release paths where cloning is unnecessary. A memory allocation failure here causes iter->err = -ENOMEM, which later triggers a WARN in nft_map_deactivate.

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces pipapo_maybe_clone() which checks for an existing clone and returns NULL on allocation failure. The walk function (nft_pipapo_walk) now calls pipapo_maybe_clone() and returns -ENOMEM if the clone is NULL, instead of unconditionally using priv->clone. Similarly, insert and deactivate paths also handle NULL return. This removes the unconditional clone operation that caused the WARN splat in nft_map_deactivate, thus fixing the vulnerability.
